title: Defending an Architecture Decision Under a Changed Constraint
objective: Defend a previously written ADR live against a skeptical reviewer, then revise it in response to one deliberately changed constraint.
whyThisMatters: A decision that only survives when nobody pushes back isn't a decision, it's a guess that hasn't been tested yet. Being able to revise a specific decision when a specific constraint changes, without rewriting everything from scratch, is the difference between an architect and someone who happened to be right once.
evidence: The original ADR plus a superseding or amended ADR responding to the mentor's changed constraint
Notes from the defense session naming the specific question that most challenged the original decision
A diff or side-by-side note showing exactly what changed between the two ADRs and why
acceptanceCriteria: A second ADR marks the first as superseded or amended, rather than replacing it silently.
The revision addresses the specific changed constraint raised in the defense, not a generic rewrite.
The notes name at least one question the apprentice could not fully answer during the defense.
